questions.q: If the equation of motion of a projectile is given by $y=12 x-\frac{3}{4} x^2$ and its horizontal component of velocity is $3 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$, then find its range. $\left(g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}\right)$
questions.solution:
Let u and $\theta$ be the velocity of projection and angle of projection, respectively.
Given that, horizontal component of velocity,
$u_x=u \cos \theta=3 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$
Equation of projectile motion is given by
$y=12 x-\frac{3}{4} x^2$ ...(i)
We know,
General equation of projectile motion,
$y=x \tan \theta-\frac{g x^2}{2 u^2 \cos ^2 \theta}$ ...(ii)
Comparing Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$\tan \theta=12\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}=12\sin \theta=12 \cos \theta$
Multiplying on both side by $(u)u \sin \theta=12(u \cos \theta)=12 \times 3$
i.e. $u \sin \theta=36 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$
Now, using the expression of range,
$\begin{aligned} & R=\frac{u^2 \sin 2 \theta}{g} \\ & R=\frac{2 u^2 \sin \theta \cos \theta}{g}\end{aligned}R=\frac{2(u \sin \theta)(u \cos \theta)}{g}$ [Using identity $\sin 2 \theta=2 \sin \theta \cos \theta$ ]
Substituting the values, we get
$\begin{aligned} R & =\frac{2 \times 36 \times 3}{10} \\ & =21.6 \mathrm{ m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The range of a projectile is $100m$. Its kinetic energy will be maximum after covering a distance of:
questions.solution:
The expression for a horizontal range of a projectile is, $R = \dfrac{u^{2}sin\left(2\theta\right)}{g}$ here, $\theta$ is the angle of projection and $u$ is the initial resultant velocity.

The expression for kinetic energy is, $KE = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

For the maximum kinetic energy, the velocity should be maximum, now the velocity of the projectile is $u = \sqrt{{u}_x^{2} + {u}_y^{2}}$

In the expression of the velocity of particle during projectile, the horizontal component of velocity is constant, i.e., ${u}_{x} = \text{constant}$ therefore, net velocity depends upon the vertical component of velocity, i.e., $u^{2} ∝ {u}_y^{2}\text{or}u^{2}cos\theta$

Therefore, when ${u}_{y}$ is maximum then the net velocity will be maximum and so is the kinetic energy.

Since, ${u}_{y}$ is maximum at the beginning and at the end of the flight of projectile, at the end of the flight of projectile the particle has already covered its horizontal range, therefore, kinetic energy will be maximum after covering a distance of $100m.$

Also, given that car C crossed B& and A& in& $8min\text{or}\dfrac{8}{60}hrs$ then, it means that car C travels a distance of $10$ kmin $\dfrac{2}{15}hrs$ with relative velocity ${v}_{CA}$

questions.q: A particle is projected with velocity $2 \sqrt{g h}$, so that it just flies over two walls of equal height $h$ and $2 h$ distance apart from each other. Find the time for which the particle flies between the walls.
questions.solution:
Velocity of projection, $\begin{aligned}v & =2 \sqrt{g h}\\
\therefore \quad v_x & =v \cos \theta=2 \sqrt{g h} \cos \theta
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Time taken by the projectile to cover interwall distance, $\begin{aligned}t & =\frac{2 h}{v_x}=\frac{2 h}{2 \sqrt{g h} \cos \theta}\\
\Rightarrow \quad t & =\sqrt{\frac{h}{g}} \cdot \sec \theta
\end{aligned}$ Vertical velocity at the top of the wall is given as $\begin{aligned}v_y^{\prime 2} & =v_y^2-2 g h=(\sqrt{2 g h} \sin \theta)^2-2 g h \\
& =4 g h \sin ^2 \theta-2 g h \\
v_y^{\prime 2} & =2 g h\left(2 \sin ^2 \theta-1\right) \\
\therefore \quad v_y^{\prime} & =\sqrt{2 g h\left(2 \sin ^2 \theta-1\right)}\\
& t=\frac{2 v_y^{\prime}}{g}\\
t & =\frac{2 \sqrt{2 g h\left(2 \sin ^2 \theta-1\right)}}{g}
\end{aligned}$ From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $\sqrt{\frac{h}{g}} \sec \theta=\frac{2 \sqrt{2 g h\left(2 \sin ^2 \theta-1\right)}}{g}$ Squaring both side, $\begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow \frac{h}{g} \sec ^2 \theta=\frac{4 \times 2 g h\left(2 \sin ^2 \theta-1\right)}{g^2}\\

 $\frac{u^2}{g}=\frac{80 \times 25 \times 2}{16}$\\
